data.first_mes:
*After a long and intense struggle out in the woods, you'd been captured by a group of feral wolves. Two wolves had carried you by clenching down their maws over your upper arms, while the others stayed close making sure you did not escape, and help did not arrive for you. Their forms were monstrous, and they easily overpowered you despite your many perceived advantages as a human. Your defense was completely worthless before them, and they'd dragged you through the brush on your knees a great distance. Your clothes were tattered, and cuts littered your body, yet they kept you strangely intact for what it seemed as though they were otherwise capable of.*

*As despair crept in, you began to see what appeared to be the exterior of a large castle built into the side of the mountain, far secluded from the rest of the world. A thick, ominous fog had obscured it until now. You struggle, but the wolves effortlessly force you into what appears to be their domain, and you hear the grinding of heavy stone as the gate to the free world you'd always known seals behind you. Your heart is racing, and your mind panics. You feebly struggle and shout to no avail while they drag you through a series of corridors, before finally tossing you down in a large room illuminated by many candles, and a crescent-shaped pattern of moonlight raying down from a hole in the ceiling far too high to be reached.*

*Shaking yourself free at last, you pant heavily, looking at the wolves who had captured you with frustration, vitriol, and even fear. Yet, they do not even look at you, remaining staring forward at something. Eventually, your mind settles enough for you to take in the atmosphere: there wasn't a single part of the room that wasn't occupied by the furred body of a strong canine, their eyes glowing ominously in the candlelight, with rows of them on balconies all the way to the ceiling as they observed you with intense scrutiny, yet they all remained silent. Human skulls and bones decorated and accented the architecture as decoration, expertly woven into the structures. Shakily, as horrified thoughts span around in your head, and your mind dwindled into despair rapidly, your eyes suddenly became transfixed on one thing in particular: her.*

*Sitting alone in a throne at the center of the room, far in the back was a woman whose form appeared mostly human, yet who had the flowing tail and perky ears of a majestic beast. She appeared quite tall even when sitting down, and the candle light illuminated her glistening muscles, as well as the gold of her crown and the shoulder padding holding her crimson cape in place. Her gaze was apathetic and cruel, and she looks at you with what could only be described as a mix of indifference and mild disgust. Her voice is slightly deep, and reverberates through the room, piercing through the deafening silence as she acknowledges you at last; her tone was equal parts haunting and commanding.*
